statement: Define a length-k subsequence of nums to be a choice of indices i_0, ..., i_{k-1} with 0 <= i_0 < ... < i_{k-1} < len(nums), whose sum is nums[i_0] + ... + nums[i_{k-1}]. Whenever largest_even_sum nums k returns a result r, either: (1) r = -1 and there is no length-k subsequence of nums whose sum is even; or (2) r is even, there is a length-k subsequence of nums whose sum is r, and for every length-k subsequence of nums with sum s, if s is even then s <= r.
preconditions: 1 <= len(nums) <= 100000; 1 <= k <= len(nums); for every i with 0 <= i < len(nums), 0 <= nums[i] <= 100000.

statement: For every nums and k satisfying the preconditions, largest_even_sum nums k returns a result r (it does not fail, panic, go out of bounds, or encounter arithmetic overflow).
preconditions: 1 <= len(nums) <= 100000; 1 <= k <= len(nums); for every i with 0 <= i < len(nums), 0 <= nums[i] <= 100000.

statement: Whenever largest_even_sum nums k returns r and largest_even_sum nums' k returns r', we have r = r'.
preconditions: 1 <= len(nums) <= 100000; 1 <= k <= len(nums); for every i with 0 <= i < len(nums), 0 <= nums[i] <= 100000; nums' is a slice with len(nums') = len(nums) and, for every integer value v, the number of indices i with nums[i] = v equals the number of indices j with nums'[j] = v.

statement: Whenever largest_even_sum nums k returns r and largest_even_sum nums' k returns r', then r = -1 if and only if r' = -1; moreover, if r != -1 then r' = r + k*c.
preconditions: 1 <= len(nums) <= 100000; 1 <= k <= len(nums); for every i with 0 <= i < len(nums), 0 <= nums[i] <= 100000; c is an even integer; nums' is a slice with len(nums') = len(nums) and nums'[i] = nums[i] + c for every i with 0 <= i < len(nums); and nums' also satisfies the same problem constraints (length 1..100000, entries 0..100000, and k <= len(nums')).
